taxonomy.note: Accepted current Kew species. Williamson County has a detailed var. laevigata treatment; Travis County is represented in the UT herbarium county flora; Val Verde County is explicitly vouchered in the Amistad vascular-plant inventory.

target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; no broad range inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaf surface and margins. Sugarberry usually has relatively smooth, thinner leaves with an oblique base and only modest teeth, rather than the strongly rough, net-veined look of netleaf hackberry. It is also an unarmed tree, unlike spiny hackberry.
diagnostic_traits: leaves relatively smooth/glabrous above at maturity
margins entire to shallowly toothed, especially toward the tip
small drupes borne singly on slender pedicels
